definitions.explanation: Describes a person or attitude that hides the truth or misrepresents it. Also used as a noun for dishonesty itself.

examples.japanese: {不正直|ふしょうじき}な{人|ひと}は{嫌|きら}いだ。
{数字|すうじ}を{隠|かく}すのは{不正直|ふしょうじき}だと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think hiding the numbers is dishonest.

examples.japanese: {一度|いちど}{不正直|ふしょうじき}な{態度|たいど}を{取|と}ると、{信用|しんよう}を{取|と}り{戻|もど}すのに{長|なが}い{時間|じかん}がかかる。
examples.english: Once you take a dishonest attitude, it takes a long time to win back trust.

notes:
The prefix {不|ふ} (not) attached to {正直|しょうじき} (honest). Somewhat bookish; in everyday speech Japanese speakers more often say うそをつく (to lie) or ずるい (sneaky, unfair).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不正直|ふしょうじき}な{人|ひと}: a dishonest person
- {不正直|ふしょうじき}な{態度|たいど}: a dishonest attitude
- {不正直|ふしょうじき}な{商売|しょうばい}: dishonest business practices

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {正直|しょうじき}: honest — the direct opposite, and a far more common word
- ずるい: sly, unfair — everyday and emotional; about taking unfair advantage rather than lying
- {嘘|うそ}つき: liar — a noun for the person, blunter and more accusing
